name: Eisirt

attributes.attribute: a poet of the otherworld and a servant of king Iubdán
an unbreakable demand, here that the king taste Ulster's porridge

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Eisirt is a figure of Irish lore. He is a poet of the Otherworld. Some bards there hold more power than human poets. Eisirt serves Iubdán, the king of the fay host. The king boasted that Ulster was full of giants. Eisirt proved the claim false. He went to Ulster and returned with the poet Áeda. That man stood small next to the fairy folk. Keen to see, king Iubdán set out with his tiny wife. Eisirt then laid a geis on his lord. Before the next dawn the king must eat the porridge that Fergus mac Léthi prepared.

okr.objective: Relay the tale of Eisirt, a poet whose jest bound his king with a geis.
key_results: Eisirt serves Iubdán, the king of the fairy host.
He proved Ulster was not a realm of giants by bringing back the dwarf poet Áeda.
He bound the king by geis to eat the Ulster porridge Fergus made before dawn.
The king then set out for Ulster with his tiny wife.
